series-inkhaven-negative-space::13.snippetHtml: [^1]: None of them responded when I asked them directly, but I’m charitable.

series-inkhaven-over-the-moon::0.title: Over the moon (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-over-the-moon::0.snippetHtml: On April 13, 1970, an oxygen tank exploded on the service module of Apollo 13. So instead of orbiting and landing on the moon as planned, they precariously set themselves up to sling around it and back to Earth on a free return trajectory.

series-inkhaven-over-the-moon::1.title: Over the moon (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-over-the-moon::1.snippetHtml: Today, after 53 years of lunar unadventure, the Artemis II mission is scheduled to launch. Unlike all the other Apollo missions that flew to the moon but did not land, Artemis II will not orbit. It’ll do a free return. Planned, this time.

series-inkhaven-over-the-moon::2.title: Over the moon (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-over-the-moon::2.snippetHtml: Yesterday, I left Montréal and arrived at Lighthaven to participate in Inkhaven. One short hop to Toronto, one six-hour flight to SFO, one hour-and-some BART ride to Berkeley. This presented somewhat less of a legroom problem than spending 10 days in space, tinned and ballistic.

series-inkhaven-over-the-moon::3.title: Over the moon (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-over-the-moon::3.snippetHtml: Among other things, astronauts are chosen for their exceptional stability. They need to execute complex and repetitive procedures for hours, and make only minimal, recoverable errors. Preferably no errors. When an accident happens, they need to keep performing. They must not be overcome by fear. To an astronaut, panic is not just a sense of impending doom. It is impending doom.

series-inkhaven-over-the-moon::4.title: Over the moon (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-over-the-moon::4.snippetHtml: I’m used to being scared, so it comes as a mild surprise to find I am not, now that I’m here. Actually I'm rather elated. What’s different from my visit to Lighthaven last June? I was much more nervous then...

series-inkhaven-over-the-moon::5.title: Over the moon (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-over-the-moon::5.snippetHtml: Maybe it’s that this trip has more of a coherent intention behind it. Or, that the small-ish size of the cohort means there’s less prospect of interacting with an endless stream of strangers, than at Manifest.

series-inkhaven-over-the-moon::6.title: Over the moon (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-over-the-moon::6.snippetHtml: Maybe it’s because I did some squats in the gym this morning. Or, that I no longer drink any alcohol. Or that I’m finally able to keep to no more than 50 mg of caffeine per day, no matter any naive impulse to grab for more of its frenetic energy, and pay the tiresome price when it wears off.

series-inkhaven-over-the-moon::7.title: Over the moon (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-over-the-moon::7.snippetHtml: Maybe it’s that I was in a good mood last night, and set the stage with a couple of easy and fun conversations with some new people. How did I manage that, though?

series-inkhaven-over-the-moon::8.title: Over the moon (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-over-the-moon::8.snippetHtml: Probably it’s all of it, all the little things I’ve done to make myself gradually more the sort of person calm enough to just keep moving.

series-inkhaven-over-the-moon::9.title: Over the moon (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-over-the-moon::9.snippetHtml: I don’t know how the Artemis mission will turn out, or if it will even launch today. Nor do I know if I’ll succeed at this new adventure I’ve joined: every day this month, I have to post 500 words or be kicked to the curb.

series-inkhaven-over-the-moon::10.title: Over the moon (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-over-the-moon::10.snippetHtml: I feel confident I can do it. Mostly. Still, there’s nothing that says I cannot fail, consumed in some terrible fire. My confidence says that’s melodrama. It also points out I might be pleasantly surprised by the attention I get.

series-inkhaven-over-the-moon::11.title: Over the moon (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-over-the-moon::11.snippetHtml: Would you take a writer seriously, if they said they weren’t in it for attention? Certainly the pursuit of truth and beauty and justice are worth the words. But how much does it matter, if someone does not read them? Going to the moon without cameras? Absurd!

series-inkhaven-over-the-moon::12.title: Over the moon (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-over-the-moon::12.snippetHtml: So yes, this is about attention. And consistency. And not being overcome by fear. Yet taken off from home, on my comparatively puny mission to learn to better share with you, there are moments I nervously wonder: might I blow up?

series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.title: Some features of a good poet (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.snippetHtml: I love writing metric poetry. During my time at Inkhaven, I’ve performed a few of my poems for some of the other writing residents. The consensus – my ego is pleased to report – is that I’m unusually good at it. I’ve been asked more than once to explain how. Here are some factors.

series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.title: Some features of a good poet (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.snippetHtml: Have something to say

series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.title: Some features of a good poet (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.snippetHtml: I almost left this one out. It’s personal and hard to explain. Maybe you want to express some different things than me. But you need to start with something to express.

series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.title: Some features of a good poet (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.snippetHtml: For me, a poem begins as a vibe and maybe some pairs of rhyming words. The story only becomes clear once it’s half-written. I’ve discussed this process before.

series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.title: Some features of a good poet (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.snippetHtml: Rhythmic sense

series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.title: Some features of a good poet (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.snippetHtml: I’ve been learning the piano for two decades. I can tap my fingers at all kinds of regular rhythms, syncopated rhythms, and polyrhythms. I have a sense of how beats build into musical phrases.

series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.title: Some features of a good poet (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.snippetHtml: It’s a basic skill that transfers from music to poetry. It feels similar in both cases. Syllables are beats, stressed or unstressed, that build into verses.

series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.title: Some features of a good poet (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.snippetHtml: I don’t think I’m exceptional among musicians. I’ve just trained more than the average writer. You could, too.

series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.title: Some features of a good poet (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.snippetHtml: Choice of words

series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.title: Some features of a good poet (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.snippetHtml: After getting some feedback from Scott Alexander and other mentors at Inkhaven, I’ve been trying not to use so many “big” words in some of my posts. It’s unnecessary and confusing for readers who might not share my semantic proclivities.

series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.title: Some features of a good poet (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.snippetHtml: Poetry’s different. Some poems might only use single-syllable words, for effect. Others are more ornate, like Persian carpets. The choice of words alters the flavour. Some people might dislike the flavour of some poems. That’s expected.

series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.title: Some features of a good poet (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.snippetHtml: Vocabulary is also trainable. The best way to train is to enjoy reading authors who are good at using many words. They don’t need to be poets; the word-choice skill transfers between prose and poetry.

series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.title: Some features of a good poet (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.snippetHtml: You can even invent your own words,[^1] though I suggest you spend thirty years on a mountaintop using all the words that already exist, before you try to do that.

series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.title: Some features of a good poet (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.snippetHtml: Word choice interacts in complicated ways with rhythm. Synonyms might not have the same number of syllables, or the same stresses; you can’t just swap them out. They might not rhyme, and they might not be made of similar sounds. All of these things affect the local flavour of verses. As far as I can tell, the only way to train for this interaction is to write poems and see how it feels to edit them.

series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.title: Some features of a good poet (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.snippetHtml: A bird in your brain

series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.title: Some features of a good poet (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.snippetHtml: When the same word is repeated many times, you start to perceive it as meaningless meaningless meaningless meaningless meaningless meaningless meaningless meaningless meaningless meaningless meaningless meaningless. It’s no longer a meaningful whole, but instead simple chain of sounds.

series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.title: Some features of a good poet (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.snippetHtml: For me, words disintegrate into sounds almost instantly. For example, I was discussing this post with Alec Thompson and he used the term “Common English”. I understood him, but “Comma Ninglish” also spontaneously appeared in my mind.

series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.title: Some features of a good poet (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.snippetHtml: As a child I experienced palilalia, or strong urges to repeat certain phrases. I’d get hooked on some nonsense like “zoobledy bop”. After a week or a month (zoobledy bop!) I’d switch over to a new bit of nonsense (tinch harst!). It wasn’t completely involuntary – more of a sudden internal excitement that would be relieved once I said the nonsense. Otherwise, the urge dissipated more slowly.

series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.title: Some features of a good poet (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.snippetHtml: As an adult I have more equanimity, and no difficulty controlling the urges, which are less frequent. But the tendency is still there, and it serves as a bridge between rhythm and word choice: it’s easy for me to flip between words-as-meanings and words-as-sounds. I guess this is trainable, but I didn’t really need to train it. It’s a side effect of autism or something. If I have some natural advantage, this is it.

series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.title: Some features of a good poet (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-some-features-of-a-good-.snippetHtml: Now go write some poetry

series-inkhaven-the-artificial-and-the-o.title: The artificial and the organic (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-artificial-and-the-o.snippetHtml: In the sci-fi novel The Mote in God’s Eye, on making first contact with the Motie species, human experts are baffled at the behaviour of their engineer caste[^1]. They’re savants. Everything they build is bespoke. In place of centralized production lines that spam the Motie masses with millions of the same office chair, they sculpt each seat in the form of its user. When there’s a shift in local needs, the engineers simply decompose and repurpose. The result is an organic infrastructure in which objects are ephemeral but eminently suitable to their niche, and the logistic focus is on the distribution of raw materials rather than finished goods.

series-inkhaven-the-artificial-and-the-o.title: The artificial and the organic (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-artificial-and-the-o.snippetHtml: Even more extreme are Star Trek replicators: you simply describe what you want, then it’s instantly conjured into thinghood in a flurry of sparkles. All that’s needed is a supply of raw, template matter.

series-inkhaven-the-artificial-and-the-o.title: The artificial and the organic (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-artificial-and-the-o.snippetHtml: LLMs have been compared to replicators. It may kind of seem that way, the first few times you use one: you tell it approximately what you want, then sparkles! Products!

series-inkhaven-the-artificial-and-the-o.title: The artificial and the organic (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-artificial-and-the-o.snippetHtml: Use them a few more times, and the dazzle calms down a little. They remain impressive and useful, but you start to notice they’re also idolatrous.[^2] They make idols out of context, worship them, and sometimes try to convince you that you should, too. They need coaxing away from the pretty lights they too easily sit and stare at. Perhaps they aren’t in bad company, then, when their user is so ready to believe they’ve obtained what they feel they wanted.

series-inkhaven-the-artificial-and-the-o.title: The artificial and the organic (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-artificial-and-the-o.snippetHtml: Well, in principle a frontier model might one-shot all sorts of products for you… if you supply exactly the right prompt. This is a Library of Babel sort of situation, where everything is reachable, if you could only pick out the thread that would lead you there. That’s the opposite of bespoke ease, as far as one-shot replication is concerned. Though as you might expect, reality is less extreme than Borges’ story: often the first prompt at least brings us closer to where we want to end up, and to the discerning user, suggests what path to follow next.

series-inkhaven-the-artificial-and-the-o.title: The artificial and the organic (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-artificial-and-the-o.snippetHtml: So the current centaur pairing of user with LLM doesn’t exactly make a replicator, but instead a kind of high-dimensional sculptor. The LLM does the chiseling. The user stands back and says, “Why haven’t you drawn the rest of the owl yet? I asked you to draw an entire owl. And why does it look like it has fur instead of feathers?”.

series-inkhaven-the-artificial-and-the-o.title: The artificial and the organic (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-artificial-and-the-o.snippetHtml: I don’t imagine things will stay like this. Clearly, today’s models can better read between the lines, and make choices more autonomously, than last season’s. But how far do we want to go, inferring wishes and immediately fulfilling them? If some future, all-inferring AI concludes that I’d love the experience machine more than anything, should it just transport me there, sparkling?[^3]

series-inkhaven-the-artificial-and-the-o.title: The artificial and the organic (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-artificial-and-the-o.snippetHtml: No, I don’t think so. I don’t want to short-circuit to the ending. I want the process.[^4] I want to experience, to learn more about myself, and about all of you, and everything. I’d like to see what it’s like to live in an organic civilization, where technology everywhere is eminently suitable to human agency, and doesn’t render it simply irrelevant.

series-inkhaven-the-artificial-and-the-o.title: The artificial and the organic (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-artificial-and-the-o.snippetHtml: Though, of course, could the AI please make an end to the dying and torture and subjugation? Bound us out of the extremes of harm we might bring ourselves to. Then let us get on being our own sculptors for a while.

series-inkhaven-the-artificial-and-the-o.title: The artificial and the organic (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-artificial-and-the-o.snippetHtml: Although the experience of a separate self is illusory, it seems to be a natural stage in the development of consciousness, just like adolescence, or being an infant. You don't look back and go "why was I ever an infant, that was silly, I should have just skipped over that stage".

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: I drafted this post in ~12h while at Inkhaven. I’ve already received some feedback about it, and since I don’t have time at the moment to do a larger edit, here’s a disclaimer: Nutrition science is riddled with evidence gaps and methodological difficulties. The purpose of this post is to enumerate mechanisms, and in particular one mechanism that may have been neglected so far. It’s following some of the paths in the causal network, but I don’t have the evidence to say in every case whether and when those paths are practically relevant. That’s why I present the novel mechanism as “this is probably fake”. I don’t mean that it’s simply worth ignoring, only that many causal paths we might propose will end up not being very important, or only important in special cases that remain to be examined. Still, it is good to start by enumerating the possibilities.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: Also, the citation links in this post are temporarily broken, but you can still find the respective numbered references at the bottom.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: Eating fruit is good, right?

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: Let’s explore how some substances[^1] commonly found in plants might make someone think twice about eating another cup of berries, and how they are probably wrong to worry about it.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: Then, I’ll propose a novel mechanism which if true, might strike fear into your breakfast.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: In 1973, the pediatric allergist Ben Feingold proposed to the American Medical Association that dietary salicylates[^2] worsen ADHD symptoms in children [1]. Therefore, he promoted a salicylate elimination diet. Many plant foods contain salicylate [2,3,4]: around 1-5 mg per 100 g for fresh fruits, up to ~35 mg per 100 g for dried fruits, and a whopping ~1 g per 100 g for spices like cumin, turmeric, rosemary, and ginger. Feingold’s fruit-fearing diet would avoid them all.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: And your average psychiatrist might have recommended it even today, if it weren’t for a 1983 meta-analysis [5] of 23 studies of the Feingold diet that found effect sizes of 0.015 and 0.052 on scales measuring attention and disruptive behaviour. Statistically speaking this is pathetic, and afterwards, most researchers abandoned the salicylate-ADHD connection.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: There’s one valid and lasting take on salicylate intolerance. This one’s inflammatory, rather than neuropsychiatric: some people with asthma or other inflammatory conditions see their symptoms worsen when they take aspirin or other non-selective NSAIDs, like ibuprofen or naproxen. In the case of asthma, this is called aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease (AERD) [6].

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: The mechanism? NSAIDs inhibit the enzyme cyclooxygenase (COX).[^3] This reduces the conversion of arachidonic acid to prostaglandins, which have both inflammatory and anti-inflammatory effects depending on context; the inflammatory cases are the ones helped by NSAIDs. But then more arachidonic acid is available for conversion by another enzyme, arachidonate 5-lipoxygenase (5-LOX). 5-LOX is the rate-limiting step in the production of leukotrienes, which also serve as inflammatory signals; there is an extra synergy in that PGE2, one of the prostaglandins synthesized by COX-1 and blocked by NSAIDs, serves an anti-inflammatory role by putting the brakes on 5-LOX. Usually all of these concerns are clinically insignificant next to the anti-inflammatory effect of reducing prostaglandins. But for those with AERD, it’s a problem:[^4]

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: 1. Eosinophils and mast cells, which are specific types of immune cells, participate in a positive feedback loop where they are recruited and activated by leukotrienes, and also produce more of them.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: Eosinophils and mast cells, which are specific types of immune cells, participate in a positive feedback loop where they are recruited and activated by leukotrienes, and also produce more of them.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: 1. The cysteinyl leukotrienes LTD4 and LTC4, downstream of 5-LOX, act on CysLT1 receptors causing airway constriction, tissue edema, and mucus production.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: The cysteinyl leukotrienes LTD4 and LTC4, downstream of 5-LOX, act on CysLT1 receptors causing airway constriction, tissue edema, and mucus production.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: 1. Through the positive feedback loop of 1, mast cells tend to activate explosively, roping in their neighbours and suddenly dumping a bunch of histamine. This can worsen lung inflammation and also cause additional allergy-like symptoms such as hives and itching. However, antihistamines alone are not sufficient to treat AERD, suggesting this is a secondary mechanism.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: Why this becomes problematic in patients with AERD is not well understood, but looks like it follows from an infection-induced epigenetic shift in the baseline balance of production of leukotrienes versus prostaglandins, and the reactivity of immune cells.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: Should dietary salicylates also be a problem for AERD? They don’t inhibit COX-1 enough to reduce the production of PGE-2 significantly, taking the brakes off 5-LOX, nor do they inhibit COX enough overall to much increase free arachidonic acid.[^5] So mechanistically, we might expect the answer to be no. The largest RCT [26] that suggests otherwise is too weak to convince.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: So: the asthmatics probably need not fear the berries. Well, not on account of their asthma, anyway.[^6]

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: I’m not going to review the entire cursed realm of internet users claiming to be sensitive to dietary salicylates, polyphenols, and whatever other Trojan berry adversaries that might be captivating their paranoia. But here’s a mugshot. In it we see people:

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: • Attributing all kinds of symptoms to dietary salicylates including dark undereye circles and adrenal fatigue.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: • Fixating on a handful of studies from the 1990s (mostly in autistic children) suggesting that phenol sulfotransferase deficiency is responsible for the accumulation of dietary phenols in the body.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: • Failing to rigorously distinguish between polyphenols, salicylates, and phenols in general, let alone different polyphenols, instead lumping everything into “high-phenol” foods. Likewise the recommended treatments for salicylate sensitivity, phenol sensitivity, and methylation disorders more or less overlap.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: Of course, in the proud tradition of giving the deranged more material to work with, I’m going to do a bit of my own speculation now, and suggest what I believe is a novel mechanism by which the consumption of salicylate- or polyphenol-containing foods might make someone anxious, stressed, agitated, aggressive, or otherwise affect their mood, and in fact how salicylic acid and polyphenols might be synergistic in this respect.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: What I am about to propose is probably fake. Like, I’ve eaten a cup of blueberries before and become anxious afterwards. Okay, maybe there’s a connection there. But it does not need to be the one that I’m proposing. Probably the blueberries were just an easy scapegoat. And me, just someone who used to have moderate baseline anxiety yearning to be accounted for.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: Now consider:

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: 1. Salicylates might increase brain dopamine synthesis. A single unreplicated study [7] in 2018 found that when mice were given 2 mg/kg/day of aspirin for 30 days, it increased the expression of tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) by 2-3x in the substantia nigra, one of the two major midbrain nuclei where dopamine is synthesized. The upstream mechanism involves the phosphorylation of CREB, one of the classic ways gene expression is regulated in animals.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: Salicylates might increase brain dopamine synthesis. A single unreplicated study [7] in 2018 found that when mice were given 2 mg/kg/day of aspirin for 30 days, it increased the expression of tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) by 2-3x in the substantia nigra, one of the two major midbrain nuclei where dopamine is synthesized. The upstream mechanism involves the phosphorylation of CREB, one of the classic ways gene expression is regulated in animals.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: 1. Some polyphenols inhibit the sole dopamine-degrading enzyme found in prefrontal cortex (PFC). Multiple studies [8,9] have shown that some common fruit polyphenols inhibit the enzyme catechol-O-methyltransferase (COMT), which metabolizes dopamine and thus controls dopamine levels. In most areas COMT isn’t the only enzyme that does this. But in PFC, it is! [12,13] This means that, if any of those polyphenols can reach PFC in sufficient concentration, it should increase the concentration of dopamine there by reducing its degradation by COMT.

Multiple studies [8,9] have shown that some common fruit polyphenols inhibit the enzyme catechol-O-methyltransferase (COMT), which metabolizes dopamine and thus controls dopamine levels. In most areas COMT isn’t the only enzyme that does this. But in PFC, it is! [12,13] This means that, if any of those polyphenols can reach PFC in sufficient concentration, it should increase the concentration of dopamine there by reducing its degradation by COMT.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: 1. Increased dopamine in prefrontal cortex pushes us away from inattentiveness, and towards rumination. The mainline theory of the relationship of PFC dopamine levels to psychology is the inverted-U model [19]: agonism of dopamine D1 receptors on pyramidal neurons enhances NMDA (excitatory) channel currents and suppresses other inputs to the neuron. This strengthens whichever representations are currently active, while reducing updating based on new inputs. This framing says that when PFC dopamine levels are too low, you get ADHD-like poor working memory because representations are wispy and transient, and this is the major hypothesis about how psychostimulants like amphetamine improve working memory in ADHD. On the other hand, too much dopamine and you tend to become ruminative and unable to stop thinking about whatever you’re currently thinking about. Downstream of that: anxiety, agitation, and whatever else.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: 1. Dopamine content/degradation in PFC varies between individuals. There are significant differences in COMT activity between individuals, due in part to the Val158Met polymorphism. Individuals with the Met/Met variant (about 25% of Europeans [10]) naturally have 3-4x lower enzymatic activity [10,11] and we might expect them to be more ruminative even prior to the addition of inhibitors.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: So: if your fruit contains a COMT-inhibiting polyphenol which can make it into PFC, it could raise the dopamine levels there and shift you towards ruminative on the inattentive-ruminative axis. And if your fruit contains salicylates which upregulate TH similarly to 10 mg of aspirin (which is a very low dose) then this may synergize by increasing the dopamine supplied to PFC. And the magnitude of the effect should depend on your baseline expression of COMT, which depends on your genes.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: There are a few potential problems here:

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: • The 2018 TH study [7] is the product of a single lab and hasn’t been replicated yet.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: The 2018 TH study [7] is the product of a single lab and hasn’t been replicated yet.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: • Does it take 30 days for the upregulation to happen? No, it probably starts within hours. The 2018 study includes some in vitro experiments that weakly support this. And the 30 day in vivo exposure period is unsurprising; note that the mice need to be killed to do the final analysis, and in the case of a chronic nutritional intervention, steady state effects are important.

The 2018 study includes some in vitro experiments that weakly support this. series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: • Dopamine projections to PFC actually come from the ventral tegmental area (VTA), and not the substantia nigra. This is probably irrelevant as these two regions are right next to each other and identical in how CREB phosphorylation affects TH expression.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: • Do rodent studies translate to humans? Or even, do results from one transgenic mouse model translate to all mice? These are nagging questions in animal research. At least, the 2018 TH study tests two different mouse types: C57/BL6 mice, which are “normal”, and aged A53T mice, which are a model of Parkinson’s disease. Additionally, the CREB phosphorylation mechanism by which TH is upregulated is probably conserved across mammals, and we know that both aspirin and dietary salicylates cross into the brain, in humans [25]. But this is not definitive.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: • The study shows that aspirin upregulates TH. Does this apply to salicylic acid, and other dietary salicylates? We know that salicylic acid and aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) largely share mechanisms, with a significant exception being aspirin’s direct, irreversible COX inhibition which requires the extra acetyl group. More importantly, aspirin is almost entirely metabolized to salicylic acid within an hour or two [25], with salicylic acid persisting somewhat longer. The study does need to be replicated with salicylic acid, but I bet you’ll find a similar effect.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: • The dose makes the poison. Assuming dietary salicylates do upregulate TH, how much do I need to consume to do so? The 2018 TH study shows that the TH upregulation happens in a narrow dosage range. So 1 mg or 100 mg of aspirin might not have the same effect, which we might only observe for the dietary salicylate equivalent of around 10 mg of aspirin. The relevant studies are weak (n=20-40 per group) and produced by the same Scottish team [16,17]; one study measured urinary salicyluric acid, and the other, plasma salicylic acid. Their results suggest that vegetarians are similar to people taking 75 mg/day of aspirin, whereas non-vegetarians are perhaps a third of that. Everyone was Scottish and the vegetarians came from a monastery, and we might not expect quite the same results for an average American. But overall these studies roughly accord with expectations, and the equivalent of 10 mg/day probably accounts for a non-negligible subset of most populations.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: On the off-chance that this “salicylate and/or polyphenols cause too much PFC dopamine and thus rumination” hypothesis is actually relevant, one of its strengths is that it would validate that some people do experience adverse effects from fruit, while also potentially explaining (say, because they have low COMT activity to begin with) why they are so fixated on whatever explanations they can scrounge up to clothe their miseries. Of course, other mechanisms may still contribute in parallel.[^7]

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: This post is a speculative review of potential mechanisms. There’s plenty of uncertainty remaining about which mechanisms are practically relevant, about the validity of unreplicated results, and about parameters like dose and timing. And now I’ll finish with a couple of general issues we haven’t covered yet.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: First, there are significant differences in salicylate content for each specific food source. We should assume that a blueberry will contain different levels of particular salicylates and polyphenols depending on growing conditions, cultivars, regions, and estimation methods.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: Second, leaving aside concerns about mechanism and replication, probably the greatest source of variability remaining is the absorption and distribution of dietary polyphenols. Many polyphenols have low bioavailability [23][^8], especially because they are actively yeeted back out of the intestinal wall by the bouncer (P-glycoprotein) right after absorption.[^9] Likewise, many polyphenols act as prebiotics for gut microbes, and it might be the metabolites that are actually relevant here, and which would need to be assayed in vivo if we wanted to be thorough about it.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: Well, there it is. Are you afraid yet? You shouldn’t be. Fruit is probably mostly fine for you.

For sedentary individuals, anyway.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: [^2]: “Salicylates” includes the drug aspirin, a.k.a. acetylsalicylic acid. Aspirin in particular is dangerous to give to children, as it can cause Reye’s syndrome, but this is probably specific to aspirin and there’s no evidence to suggest it applies to dietary salicylates.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: [^3]: There are two active forms of COX, COX-1 and COX-2. Different NSAIDs have different selectivity for one or the other. Aspirin prefers COX-1, especially at low doses. Naproxen is about equally balanced. Ibuprofen slightly prefers COX-2. Diclofenac and all the drugs in the coxib family are COX-2 selective. COX-1 inhibition is antithrombotic (by reducing production of thromboxane A2) but is also largely responsible for negative effects of NSAIDs on the gut, which is why aspirin is the most cardioprotective but also the most stomach-melting of the bunch. COX-2 inhibition is primarily anti-inflammatory, and while the absence of COX-1 inhibition by coxibs means they are comparatively gut-safe, it is also pro-thrombotic (due to reducing production of prostacyclin while sparing thromboxane A2) and thus increases the risk of cardiovascular adverse events with chronic use.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: This all points to a pathological attractor state; a self-reinforcing equilibrium in the system dynamics. It’s uncertain which of these doors leads to the attractor in the first place. It does seem it’s not strictly congenital, but tends to arise in a patient’s 30s or 40s following a severe upper respiratory infection, suggesting an epigenetic trigger.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: [^5]: Salicylic acid is similarly anti-inflammatory to aspirin, but probably by a combination of different upstream mechanisms, such as inhibition of IκB kinase β → less NF-κB production [21], and less downstream upregulation of COX-2 conditional on being in an inflammatory state. But ultimately aspirin shares these mechanisms, as it’s partly metabolized to salicylic acid.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: [^6]: Plants contain other substances which might be relevant (but probably aren’t):

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: • Several polyphenols inhibit 5-LOX in vitro. A very weak (n=11, uncontrolled, 4-week longitudinal) pilot study [14] showed decreased 5-LOX activation and reduced production of leukotrienes by eosinophils, in participants consuming 100 mg/day of soy isoflavones for 4 weeks. A later, stronger RCT (n=386, placebo-controlled, 24 weeks) [15] returned a negative result for asthma measures, even after verifying that the crucial isoflavone genistein was present at plasma levels sufficient to match in vitro inhibition conditions, suggesting either that the polyphenol was not entering eosinophils from plasma, or else that 5-LOX inhibition is inadequate to control asthma. And anyway, 100 mg/day of isoflavones is equivalent to about a pound of tofu, or 5-10 cups of soy milk.

And anyway, 100 mg/day of isoflavones is equivalent to about a pound of tofu, or 5-10 cups of soy milk.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: • Some polyphenols inhibit the enzyme COMT, which metabolizes catechols (dopamine, norepinephrine, epinephrine, and others). This could increase the half-life of circulating epinephrine → activates β2 adrenergic receptors in the lungs → dilates airways, by the same mechanism as asthma medications like salbutamol. As far as I can see this has not been tested, but I doubt it is significant as there are other mechanisms for clearing plasma epinephrine which should pick up the slack.

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: [^8]: In the case of quercetin, for example, we need to reach 1-8 µM to effectively inhibit COMT [8], but usually we can only get 0.1-0.2 µM in plasma [23].

series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.title: The Blueberries of Wrath (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-blueberries-of-wrath.snippetHtml: [^9]: P-glycoprotein serves a similar role at the blood-brain barrier, bouncing things back out. This is why loperamide, an opioid, treats diarrhea but does not get you high, and also why the antihistamine cetirizine makes you less drowsy than diphenhydramine. We expect variability here for a few reasons: 1) P-glycoprotein has different affinity for different substrates, as usual, 2) P-glycoprotein expression varies between individuals, and 3) P-glycoprotein is inhibited by certain dietary substances, such as piperine from black pepper [24].

series-inkhaven-the-one-that-loved-me-mo.snippetHtml: I don’t know what made me do it. We happened to be alone together for a few minutes, before I left with the rest. They’d all already gone out of the room for some reason or other.

series-inkhaven-the-one-that-loved-me-mo.title: The one that loved me most (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-one-that-loved-me-mo.snippetHtml: So I took her hand. And for a couple of minutes, there was calm.

series-inkhaven-the-one-that-loved-me-mo.title: The one that loved me most (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-one-that-loved-me-mo.snippetHtml: She had lost consciousness a week before. I hadn’t reached out to her since. What was the point? Was she even there to feel me? I remember reflecting at the time how out of place it seemed.

series-inkhaven-the-one-that-loved-me-mo.title: The one that loved me most (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-one-that-loved-me-mo.snippetHtml: The next morning we learned early what had happened. Not too early. Maybe we needed our sleep.

series-inkhaven-the-one-that-loved-me-mo.title: The one that loved me most (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-one-that-loved-me-mo.snippetHtml: Obvious feelings aside, I wasn’t shocked. That’s not to say I was a particularly sane or well-calibrated teenager. Just dissociated enough from my feelings that across the ample days whose daylight hours we’d lurked away in those sterile halls, the conclusion had met little resistance as it settled to the floor of my mind. Inevitable.

series-inkhaven-the-one-that-loved-me-mo.title: The one that loved me most (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-one-that-loved-me-mo.snippetHtml: My grandfather was offended when I did not cry just when he thought I should. I wonder if, grasping in vain to teach me that tears are not only possible but necessary, there was a moment when he considered that pressing harder on an insect would merely increase its resolve. You know, like a cat automatically leans into you when you nudge it.

series-inkhaven-the-one-that-loved-me-mo.title: The one that loved me most (Inkhaven)
The one that loved me most (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-one-that-loved-me-mo.snippetHtml: The last thing thing she did for me was to sing me Happy Birthday. She slurred her words. Obviously a shadow, but not a distorted one; still the shape of herself, just blurry and sleepy and slow.

series-inkhaven-the-one-that-loved-me-mo.title: The one that loved me most (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-one-that-loved-me-mo.snippetHtml: I think it was mostly the phenobarbital and the morphine and whatever other lesser evils were sparing her from unending torment and seizures.1 Tumours had long since moved into her brain, but apparently they were not pressing on the right places to erase her before she went.

series-inkhaven-the-one-that-loved-me-mo.title: The one that loved me most (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-one-that-loved-me-mo.snippetHtml: I can’t remember if she looked at me as she sung to me. I think she did. I want to assume she could still see me clearly.

series-inkhaven-the-one-that-loved-me-mo.title: The one that loved me most (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-one-that-loved-me-mo.snippetHtml: I’ve never quite been able to let it go: why did I reach out like that? Did I predict what was going to happen that night? That I should say goodbye?

series-inkhaven-the-one-that-loved-me-mo.title: The one that loved me most (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-one-that-loved-me-mo.snippetHtml: I don’t see how. Oh, I’ve ruminated on it enough. Am I forgetting something about what I perceived? Was she breathing differently? Was the look on her face subtly wrong? Or peaceful? Did the nurses sense something, and somehow telegraph it to an autistic child who could hardly look them in the eye?

series-inkhaven-the-one-that-loved-me-mo.title: The one that loved me most (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-one-that-loved-me-mo.snippetHtml: If I’d been a cat, would I have curled up beside her, like the ones that pick out all the patients on the threshold?

series-inkhaven-the-one-that-loved-me-mo.title: The one that loved me most (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-one-that-loved-me-mo.snippetHtml: I don’t know... I don’t know. There’s no record except the images in my mind, ever more distant.

series-inkhaven-the-one-that-loved-me-mo.title: The one that loved me most (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-one-that-loved-me-mo.snippetHtml: It’s been 18 years. I miss you, mom. Maybe not as much as I should. I’m a strange person, but I guess you’d be proud of me anyway.

series-inkhaven-the-one-that-loved-me-mo.title: The one that loved me most (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-the-one-that-loved-me-mo.snippetHtml: It hurts me to say that I don’t believe I’ll ever see you again. Instead, I’ve shared all these words with the part of you I keep with me. And it helped me. You helped me to say this.

series-inkhaven-two-poems::0.title: Two Poems (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-two-poems::0.snippetHtml: Today, I want to write about poetry. I did not accept this until Cate Hall’s Q&A, when she repeated some things I know. Some obvious things I’d apparently forgotten, for a moment.

series-inkhaven-two-poems::1.title: Two Poems (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-two-poems::1.snippetHtml: So, let me share two poems with you. I wrote one last year, and one today. Each is followed with a bit of explanation about its form, and my writing process.

series-inkhaven-two-poems::3.title: Two Poems (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-two-poems::3.snippetHtml: I’ll tell you just one thing about the renga form, before the poem: each verse is only linked directly to its neighbours. There is no overarching narrative, but a sort of sausage-chain of images.

series-inkhaven-two-poems::4.title: Two Poems (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-two-poems::4.snippetHtml:
the glittering glints

of droplets on the branches
recount me your love

a forgotten sensation

of welcome fluidity

the ocean remains

in the spring, in the autumn
unfailingly vast

a fish swims and swims and swims

and swims, never gaining ground

the soil is ready

for all of us to begin
to plant our footsteps

in the garden she awaits

freedom from fertility

this child can reckon

which flowers are most suited
for a funeral

my casket: inexpensive,

unbought, unbuilt, unimagined

a mountain cabin

carefully made of wood planks
burns with the forest

some kilns stay hotter, longer,

to better fire pottery

this jug is for milk

but the cows are at pasture
and won’t be back soon

I know an animal’s mind:

an evergreen song of now

no-one can escape

the ecstatic turbulence
of unknown moments

what do we chase in our lives

but beauty, which is right here?

series-inkhaven-two-poems::19.title: Two Poems (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-two-poems::19.snippetHtml: Renga is a traditional Japanese form of alternating verses (ku) of 5-7-5 and 7-7 syllables (morae). The exact number of verses varied, but the standard was originally 100 (~1300s) and later 36 (~1600s). The form became less strict over time.

series-inkhaven-two-poems::20.title: Two Poems (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-two-poems::20.snippetHtml: It was almost always written collaboratively, typically with 3-6 participants, guided and adjudicated by a master (sabaki). The most honoured participant would write the first verse, the hokku, which should be able to stand on its own; it’s the precursor to the famous haiku form.

series-inkhaven-two-poems::21.title: Two Poems (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-two-poems::21.snippetHtml: There are some arcane rules (kigo) that govern which verses must contain references to specific objects (e.g. the moon, or cherry blossoms). There are also rules about how many verses in a row can focus on a given topic (e.g. love) before a shift has to happen.

series-inkhaven-two-poems::22.title: Two Poems (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-two-poems::22.snippetHtml: The renga I’ve shared is heterodox: I wrote it solo, and it contains only 14 verses. I didn’t follow any strong thematic constraints, or rules about the moon appearing, or whatever. It took me an hour or two to write and edit, on the day I first learned about renga (14 May 2025). It’s the only one I’ve written so far, aside from a few scattered verses with friends. I did edit the hokku, when writing this post. Here’s the original:

series-inkhaven-two-poems::23.snippetHtml:

on droplets on the sidewalk
recall me my love

series-inkhaven-two-poems::26.title: Two Poems (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-two-poems::26.snippetHtml: A nice thing about renga: it lets you practice in bite-size pieces which are not totally unhinged from each other. The thematic constraint between adjacent verses binds the poem together, but doesn’t force you to think hard about where you are going. This seems like good practice that’s specific to generating imagery and keeping it locally coherent.

series-inkhaven-two-poems::29.title: Two Poems (Inkhaven)
series-inkhaven-two-poems::29.snippetHtml:
At times I grasp my pen to summon Muses;

instead I’m met by gasping, drowning Choice,
which struggling to stay floating, self-abuses;
so ends my song before I’ve found my voice.

Now voiceless I am subject to your leering.

Your judgment is foretold, a muffled scream
that fills my future — all-conjoining fearing,
a stifling stillness, this ensqualored dream.

For what I know, and what I can accept,

stay silent in me ‘til I hear you speak
the obvious. Oh, were I more adept,
I’d spend less effort keeping myself weak.

When I release this raft to which I cling,

I listen to your love, and start to sing.
